subject.title: [Feature]: Standardize skill data directory convention (configPaths) under ~/.openclaw/

question: Should OpenClaw define a first-class per-skill writable data contract, and if so should it be a filesystem path, a plugin/skill runtime API backed by SQLite/KV, or ClawHub authoring guidance only?
rationale: The requested behavior adds a new durable storage/API convention for third-party skills, and repository policy treats config/state/plugin API surfaces as product and compatibility-sensitive rather than safe automated cleanup.

options.title: Define a core skill data contract
options.body: Add a narrow OpenClaw-owned convention or runtime helper for per-skill persistent data and document the upgrade/security behavior before implementation.

options.title: Use plugin/KV-backed storage instead
options.body: Route persistent skill data through a plugin or SDK storage surface so OpenClaw avoids creating more unmanaged filesystem state.

options.title: Keep it as ClawHub guidance
options.body: Publish authoring guidance that discourages home-root litter without adding runtime enforcement or new metadata in core.

recommendation.title: Define a core skill data contract
recommendation.body: Add a narrow OpenClaw-owned convention or runtime helper for per-skill persistent data and document the upgrade/security behavior before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The likely decision is about the skills subsystem boundary, and recent subsystem layout/centralization history makes this the best routing signal among the available owners.
